definitions.explanation: To walk around without a specific destination, often for leisure or to kill time.
To spend time in an area without doing anything particular.

examples.japanese: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は{近所|きんじょ}をぶらついている。
examples.english: On my days off, I wander around the neighborhood.

examples.japanese: デパートをぶらついて{時間|じかん}をつぶした。
examples.english: I killed time wandering around the department store.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}でぶらついている{若者|わかもの}たち。
examples.english: Young people hanging around in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {暇|ひま}だから{公園|こうえん}でぶらついていた。
examples.english: I was hanging around the park because I had nothing to do.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}もしないでぶらついてばかりいる。
examples.english: They just hang around without working.

notes:
ぶらつく is an informal verb describing aimless wandering or hanging around. It comes from the onomatopoeia ぶらぶら (dangling, swinging loosely), suggesting a relaxed, unhurried movement.

Related expressions:
- ぶらぶらする: similar meaning, to loaf around
- {散歩|さんぽ}する: to take a walk (more purposeful)

While often neutral, ぶらつく can have slightly negative connotations when describing someone who should be doing something productive.
